source_name: Karanović & Partners — North Macedonia payment services legislation updates
why_relevant: Regional law firm that publishes timely English-language analyses of MK payments legislation (adoption dates, transitional deadlines, licensing obligations). Faster and clearer than official sources for interpreting what changed and by when.

source_name: DDK Law (Skopje) — English translation/overview of the Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems
why_relevant: Local-firm English rendering of the law's structure and licence categories; useful bridge between the Macedonian statutory text and English analysis, and a check on terminology mapping (e.g. заменски надоместок = interchange fee).

source_name: Licentium — North Macedonia payments licensing hub
why_relevant: Commercial licensing-intelligence aggregator that tracks PI/EMI authorisation requirements and, in some jurisdictions, licence-holder lists. A useful secondary cross-check on the NBRSM register, but must be treated as unverified vendor content, not a primary register.

source_name: MIA / Нова Македонија / МКД.МК — instant payments and TIPS-clone coverage
why_relevant: Macedonian media relay NBRSM statements on joining the ECB/TIPS-based instant-payments initiative (with reported timing alongside Albania and Kosovo, following Bosnia and Montenegro). Fastest dated signal for go-live milestones, to be confirmed against NBRSM primary sources.

source_name: Bank general terms & conditions / fee tariffs as regulatory-compliance artefacts (Stopanska banka, Komercijalna banka, ProCredit, Alta, CCBank)
why_relevant: The PSPS Law forces standardised, dated publication of framework contracts, fee terms and payment-account information documents. Versioned PDFs (e.g. valid from 01.01.2026, 01.03.2026) reveal in near-real time how banks re-price cards, ATM/POS and instant transfers in response to regulation — an indirect but high-frequency read on interchange and fee policy.

source_name: NLB Banka MK — public explainer on the Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems
why_relevant: Bank-published plain-language summary of obligations arising from the law; useful for glossary/terminology validation in Macedonian and to see which provisions banks consider operationally material.

source_name: ЕСЈН — Електронски систем за јавни набавки (e-Nabavki), Public Access portal
why_relevant: Single mandatory national portal for all public contracts above MKD 500,000. Carries notices (огласи), tender documentation, contract-award notices and realized-contract records for ATM supply/maintenance, POS terminals, card personalisation, cash handling/CIT and core-banking IT bought by state bodies, municipalities, public enterprises and state-owned entities. Directly exposes vendor names, awarded values, quantities and contract durations that vendors never publish.

source_name: Биро за јавни набавки (БЈН) — Bureau of Public Procurement
why_relevant: Regulator and operator of ЕСЈН. Publishes the rulebook, CPV nomenclature guidance, manuals and — critically — aggregate statistics on procurement volumes by category and contracting authority. Pointer to the full universe of contracting authorities and to methodology needed to query ЕСЈН correctly.

source_name: Биро за јавни набавки — Годишни извештаи (annual reports on the functioning of the procurement system)
why_relevant: Yearly quantitative baseline: total value and number of contracts, breakdown by procedure type and contracting authority, e-auction usage. Gives the denominator against which any ATM/POS/cash-handling tender value can be sized, and shows year-on-year public spend trend on banking services.

source_name: Државен завод за ревизија (ДЗР) — State Audit Office, audit reports register
why_relevant: Audit reports on ministries, municipalities, public enterprises, the National Bank and state-owned financial entities routinely quantify cash handling, collection channels, card/POS acceptance costs, bank fees paid and IT procurement irregularities. Audits reveal operational volumes (number of cash points, transaction values, fee levels) that no tender notice states.

source_name: Државна комисија за жалби по јавни набавки (ДКЖЈН) — State Appeals Commission for Public Procurement
why_relevant: Publishes filed appeals daily and decisions from its sessions. Appeal files in ATM/POS/card-personalisation tenders are the richest single disclosure of competitive dynamics: which vendors bid, at what price, on what technical grounds bids were rejected, and which incumbent was protected. Often the only public evidence of losing bidders.

source_name: Народна банка на Република Северна Македонија — Јавни набавки (NBRM procurement page)
why_relevant: The central bank is itself a contracting authority and buys banknote processing/counting/sorting machines, cash vault equipment, secure cash transport, currency destruction and payment-system IT. Its tenders are a direct read on the country's cash-handling infrastructure refresh cycle and on which vendors serve the cash cycle at the apex.

source_name: АД Пошта на Северна Македонија — state-owned postal operator, procurement
why_relevant: The state-owned post is one of the country's largest cash-acceptance and bill-payment networks (postal counters, money orders, utility collection) and is the historic partner of the postal savings channel. Its procurement of counter cash-handling systems, POS terminals, cash-in-transit and counter automation is a direct proxy for non-bank cash and payment volumes. Named in the cell rationale as a key state buyer.

source_name: Министерство за финансии — Е-јавни набавки / Биро за јавни набавки pages
why_relevant: Ministry-level entry point that defines the legal frame, links ЕСЈН and БЈН, and is itself a contracting authority for treasury/payment-system procurement. Useful as an authoritative pointer and for tracking legal changes that alter what gets published.

source_name: Е-Пазар (e-Pazar) — government electronic marketplace for low-value purchases
why_relevant: Low-value public purchases (below the ЕСЈН threshold) run through the e-marketplace. Captures the long tail that ЕСЈН misses: individual POS terminals, card readers, cash counters, safes and consumables bought by small municipalities and agencies — useful for unit-price benchmarking and for spotting small local resellers.

source_name: Opentender.eu — North Macedonia country portal (Government Transparency Institute)
why_relevant: Normalises North Macedonian national-portal and TED notices into a structured, downloadable, OCDS-flavoured dataset with buyer and supplier entity pages. Solves the ЕСЈН bot-defence and SPA problem by giving bulk historical data for time-series analysis of ATM/POS/cash-handling awards and vendor market shares.

source_name: TED — Tenders Electronic Daily (EU), North Macedonia notices
why_relevant: Above-threshold and donor/IPA-funded North Macedonian notices appear on TED with a stable machine-readable API and PDF notices. Best-structured route for large ATM/POS/core-banking or IPA-funded payment-infrastructure contracts, and it names winners with values.

source_name: Центар за граѓански комуникации (ЦГК) — Center for Civil Communications, procurement monitoring
source_subtype: NGO watchdog / analytical reports + municipal database
why_relevant: The only NGO doing continuous direct monitoring of Macedonian public procurement since 2008, publishing quarterly monitoring reports and a municipal procurement database searchable from 2015. Adds interpretation, irregularity flags and per-municipality series that raw ЕСЈН records do not give, and identifies recurring incumbent suppliers.

source_name: Balkan Tender Watch — North Macedonia country section
why_relevant: Regional civil-society procurement watch aggregating Macedonian cases, legal analyses and links to national monitoring bodies. Good snowball source for further actors and for cross-border comparison of ATM/POS tender practice across the Western Balkans.

source_name: Отворена влада / ОВП портал (Open Government Partnership North Macedonia) — procurement-as-open-data commitment
why_relevant: Documents the government's binding commitments on publishing procurement as open data, including planned API/bulk releases from ЕСЈН. Tells the collector what data is due to become available and when — a forward-looking pointer that changes collection strategy.

source_name: Влада на РСМ — Јавни набавки (Government procurement page) and per-ministry procurement sections
why_relevant: Individual contracting authorities mirror their own notices, annual procurement plans and signed contracts on their own sites, sometimes with more attachment detail (technical specifications, bills of quantity) than the ЕСЈН dossier exposes anonymously. Technical specifications are where ATM models, POS terminal counts and card-personalisation volumes are actually stated.

source_name: Слободен пристап (slobodenpristap.mk) — FOI request platform, and АСПИ (Агенција за заштита на правото на слободен пристап до информации од јавен карактер)
why_relevant: Where ЕСЈН hides contract attachments or a state-owned entity does not publish, a Freedom-of-Information request under the Macedonian FOI law is a lawful escalation. The platform publishes past requests and responses, and АСПИ maintains the register of information holders — including the appeals commission and financial bodies — with named FOI officers.

source_name: Commercial tender aggregators indexing e-nabavki dossiers (tender-service.com, macedoniatenders.com, tendersontime, TenderImpulse, TenderDetail, selltostate/Hook)
why_relevant: These mirror ЕСЈН notice titles, deadlines and dossier UUIDs in plain HTML, indexable by search engines. That makes them a practical discovery layer and a workaround for the ЕСЈН 403/SPA barrier: find the dossier UUID here, then fetch the canonical ЕСЈН dossier. They also reveal the ЕСЈН URL grammar.

source_name: Invest North Macedonia — Public procurement guide (English framework overview)
why_relevant: Official English-language explanation of thresholds, procedure types and where notices are published. Useful for calibrating what falls inside/outside ЕСЈН (the MKD 500,000 threshold matters a lot for small POS purchases) and for onboarding non-Macedonian-reading analysts.

source_name: Агенција за пошти (ap.mk) — Postal Agency, licence register and sector reports
why_relevant: Regulator of the postal sector; publishes licences, network-size and opening-hours data for АД Пошта на Северна Македонија and other operators. Supplies the denominator (number of postal counters/units) needed to interpret Пошта's cash-handling and payment-acceptance procurement.

source_name: Large public enterprises and utilities as contracting authorities (ЕВН Македонија, ЈСП Скопје, ЈП за државни патишта, municipal water/heating utilities)
why_relevant: Utility and transport operators are the country's biggest non-bank cash and card collectors — counter payments, ticket vending machines, prepaid meters, bill-payment kiosks. Their tenders for payment kiosks, POS acceptance, cash-in-transit and collection-agent contracts are among the best indirect readings of retail cash-versus-card behaviour outside banking statistics. They procure through ЕСЈН as утилитетни субјекти.

source_name: World Bank Global Findex programme page and download portal
why_relevant: Master entry point to Findex reports, indicator definitions, country briefs and bulk downloads; snowballs to DataBank, microdata catalogue and methodology notes needed to interpret MK figures.

source_name: IMF FAS annual highlights reports and glossary of indicators
why_relevant: Explains definitions and breaks in ATM/POS indicators and gives regional benchmarks against which MK density can be read; essential for avoiding misinterpretation of series changes.
